accordions.heading: What are chlamydia and gonorrhoea?
accordions.content:
Chlamydia and gonorrhoea are sexually transmitted bacterial infections. They can cause symptoms such as pain when peeing or unusual discharge, but many people have no noticeable symptoms at all. Left untreated, both can cause long-term health problems, including fertility problems.

Chlamydia and gonorrhoea can be treated and cured with antibiotics.

accordions.heading: Is this for you?
accordions.content:
You don’t need to have symptoms to test. Chlamydia and gonorrhoea can cause no noticeable symptoms.

It may be worth testing if:
checklist: You have a new sexual partner, or more than one
A sexual partner has told you they have chlamydia, gonorrhoea or another STI
You have possible symptoms, such as pain when peeing or unusual discharge

benefits.heading: Test privately
benefits.text: Everything you need to test for chlamydia and gonorrhoea at home:

how.heading: How does the test work?
how.intro:
The test looks for chlamydia and gonorrhoea bacteria in a swab sample. If you have a vagina, the swab is taken from your vagina. If you have a penis, the swab is taken from just inside the opening of your urethra.

Your result appears on the test pad in around 15 minutes, with no sample to send to a laboratory.

steps.title: Take your swab
steps.text: Wash your hands and open the swab packet without touching the soft tip. Follow the collection instructions for your sample type. If you're taking a urethral swab, don't pee for at least 2 hours beforehand.

steps.title: Mix your sample
steps.text: Add 10 drops of liquid A to the sample tube, then insert your swab. Rotate it 15 times and leave it for 2 minutes. Add 10 drops of liquid B, and rotate the swab another 15 times. Leave it for 1 minute. Squeeze the tube as you remove the swab, then attach the dropper lid.

steps.title: Add your sample
steps.text: Add 3 drops of the prepared sample to the Ng sample well and 3 drops to the Ct sample well on the test pad.

steps.title: Read your result
steps.text: Read both results between 15 and 20 minutes. Don't interpret the results after 25 minutes.

windows.heading: When should I test?
windows.subheading: You can take the test at any time, but after a recent exposure it can take time for there to be enough bacteria for this test to find. If it’s been less than 2 weeks and your result is negative, test again at 2 weeks.
windows.initialTitle: Test now. If negative, repeat in 2 weeks.

groups.intro:
Read your test between 15 and 20 minutes. Don't read it after 25 minutes.

The test pad has two windows, one marked Ct (chlamydia) and one marked Ng (gonorrhoea). Read each one separately. C is the control line. T is the test line.

items.title: Negative
items.text: One line at C only, in both windows. Chlamydia and gonorrhoea were not detected.

items.title: Chlamydia positive
items.text: Lines at C and T in the Ct window, even if the T line is faint. Chlamydia was detected.

items.title: Gonorrhoea positive
items.text: Lines at C and T in the Ng window, even if the T line is faint. Gonorrhoea was detected.

items.title: Invalid
items.text: No line at C in one or both windows, even if a T line appears. The test has not worked. Contact us and we'll help.

notes.title: Good to know
notes.text: This test is designed for screening and doesn’t replace advice from a doctor or nurse. For ages 16 and over.

questions.question: How soon after sex can I test for chlamydia and gonorrhoea?
questions.answer:
You can take the test at any time, but testing too early can give a negative result even if you have chlamydia or gonorrhoea. If it has been less than 2 weeks since the sexual contact you're concerned about and your result is negative, test again once 2 weeks have passed.

If you have symptoms or a sexual partner has tested positive, contact a sexual health clinic without waiting for the 2-week mark.

questions.question: How reliable is this chlamydia and gonorrhoea rapid test?
questions.answer: Rapid tests can be reliable when used correctly.Testing too early or collecting a swab incorrectly can affect your result. If you have symptoms or are still concerned after a negative result, speak to a sexual health clinic. A positive result should be followed up with a sexual health clinic for further testing.

questions.question: What does a negative chlamydia and gonorrhoea test result mean?
questions.answer: A negative result means chlamydia and gonorrhoea were not detected by the test. If your possible exposure was within the last 2 weeks, you may have tested too early. Test again at 2 weeks. If you have symptoms or are still concerned, speak to a sexual health clinic.

questions.question: What if my result is positive?
questions.answer:
If your rapid test is positive for chlamydia, gonorrhoea or both, contact a sexual health clinic for further testing and treatment. Chlamydia and gonorrhoea are treatable and can be cured with antibiotics. NHS sexual health services are free and confidential. If an infection is confirmed, recent sexual partners may also need to be tested.

Don't have vaginal, anal or oral sex until you and your partner have completed treatment and the clinic has advised it's safe to have sex again.

questions.question: I’ve recently been treated. Can I test again?
questions.answer:
You may need another test after treatment, but the timing depends on the infection and treatment you've received.

Testing too soon can sometimes give a positive result even after successful treatment. Follow the advice of the sexual health clinic that treated you about whether and when to test again.

questions.question: Does this test check for infections in the throat or bottom?
questions.answer: No. This test only checks a swab from the vagina or the urethra. If you've had oral or anal sex, speak to a sexual health clinic about testing those areas.

questions.question: Can I take a chlamydia and gonorrhoea test while pregnant?
questions.answer: If you’re pregnant and concerned about chlamydia or gonorrhoea, speak to your midwife, GP or a sexual health clinic before taking a swab. They can test you safely and arrange treatment if needed.
